questions.problem: What is the projection of the intersection between the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8}=-1$ and the plane $y=2$ onto the $xz$-plane?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the hyperboloid and the plane $y=2$, we substitute $y=2$ into the equation of the hyperboloid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =-1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}+1-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =-1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =-2 \\ -\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the hyperbola: $-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=1.$

questions.problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets ${x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-{z}^{2}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-{z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1 & ={z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1 \\ z & =\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
{x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$

questions.problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets $(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}-\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}-\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16} & =-1 \\ (x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1 & =\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(z+5)^{2}}{16} & =(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1 \\ (z+5)^{2} & =16((x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1) \\ z+5 & =\pm 4\sqrt{(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1} \\ z & =-5\pm 4\sqrt{(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
(x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$

questions.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet $(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-(z-3)^{2}=1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-(z-3)^{2} & =1 \\ (x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-1 & =(z-3)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(z-3)^{2} & =(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-1 \\ z-3 & =\pm \sqrt{(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-1} \\ z & =3\pm \sqrt{(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}-1 & \ge 0 \\ (x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2} & \ge 1,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the circle $(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}=1,$ which includes the boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,(x+5)^{2}+{y}^{2}\ge 1\}.
$$

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the hyperboloid of two sheets $-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperboloid. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{0}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-1 \\ -\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{z}^{2} & =-1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-{z}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

which is the equation of a hyperbola in $xz$-plane.
